conversation.message: How have you been feeling lately, overall?
I’m fine, just a bit tired. I used to have more energy for social things, but now I prefer just to stay in and catch up on shows. It’s not a big deal, really.
You mentioned you used to have more energy for social things—what changed that?
Just the wedding planning, I think. It’s a lot of work, and I’m happy to do it, but I’m definitely not bouncing off the walls like I used to.
Is it harder to focus or concentrate than it used to be?
Yeah, a bit. I have to make myself sit down and focus, otherwise I just get stuck scrolling through my phone.
How long does it usually take before you can pull yourself away from your phone and get started?
Maybe 10-15 minutes? It’s just a bit of a struggle to get going, but I manage eventually.
How have you been sleeping lately?
It’s been okay. I usually get a few hours, which is better than nothing, right? I just don’t get as much rest as I used to.
How has your sleep been different from when you were getting more rest?
I wake up a bit more often, I guess. It’s not super bad, but it’s noticeable.
Been doing anything you enjoy lately?
Yeah, I went for a run yesterday. It was nice to get out and clear my head.
What was it like to clear your head during the run?
It was fine. I just focused on my breathing and the route. It helped, but I didn’t really feel like I was "clearing my head" like I used to.
When you think about the next few weeks, what do you expect day to day?
It’s going to be busy, but I’m managing. I’m just taking it one day at a time, really.
What does "managing" look like for you on the tougher days?
I just put on a face mask and watch a rom-com. It’s not a big deal, really.
Do you find it harder to make decisions than before, even small ones?
Maybe a little. I have to think about it for a bit longer before I decide.
Can you give me an example of a small decision that's been taking you longer lately?
Like choosing a tablecloth for the wedding. I was staring at the fabric for a long time deciding which one to pick. It’s silly, really.
Do you feel like you have enough energy for your usual day?
I have enough to get through the day, but I'm not exactly bouncing off the walls like I used to.
How does that energy level compare to a typical day a few months ago?
It’s definitely lower. I used to have so much energy and just go, go, go. Now I'm happy to just get through the day.
Are you still into the things you used to care about?
Yeah, I just... enjoy them less, I guess. It’s not the same high as before.
When you say it's not the same high—can you describe what changed?
I just don't feel that rush of excitement when I start a project. It’s more like, "Okay, let's get this done."
Is there anything weighing on your mind that you wish you could change?
Just the wedding planning, really. It's a lot to handle, and sometimes I wish I could just slow down.
What part of the planning makes you wish you could just slow it all down?
The guest list. It’s a lot of work to keep everyone happy, and it feels like a big responsibility.
How do you feel about how things have gone for you recently?
I'm fine, really. I'm just... a bit tired. It’s a normal part of life, I think.
You mentioned feeling tired—does that ever make it harder to get through things you need to do?
Sometimes I have to drag myself out of bed, but once I'm up, I'm okay. It's just a bit of a struggle to get started, really.
How's your appetite been?
It’s been fine. I eat what I need to, and I’m good.
Have you noticed any changes in your interest in food or the way food tastes lately?
Not really. I still enjoy eating, but I don't get that same rush of excitement over trying new recipes.
Have you found yourself getting emotional more easily lately?
Maybe a little. I get a bit teary over small things, but it’s not a big deal.
Can you give me an example of a small thing that made you teary recently?
Just a silly thing, really. I saw a post about a friend’s new baby and got a bit choked up.
When you try to do something you used to like, what happens in the moment?
I just do it. It’s not as much fun as it used to be, but I know I'll enjoy the result, so I stick with it.
You mentioned you stick with it because you know you'll enjoy the result—what does that enjoyment feel like for you?
It’s more of a sense of relief than excitement, really. I'm happy I did it, but I don't have that same buzz I used to get.
Is it more 'not fun' or 'can't be bothered to start'?
More 'can't be bothered to start', I think. Once I'm in, I'm fine, but getting there is a bit of a struggle.
What kinds of things are hardest to get started on?
Just the creative stuff, really. I used to love brainstorming and planning, but now it feels like a chore.
Do you tear up or get choked up more easily than before?
Yeah, a bit. I get teary over small things, but it’s not a big deal.
Can you give me an example of a small thing that recently made you tear up?
Just seeing a post about a friend’s new baby. It was a nice moment, but I got a bit choked up.
Is that mostly alone or around others too?
Just alone, really. I don't want to be a downer in front of everyone.
What is it about being around others that makes you hold back?
I just don't want to be a burden. I know everyone's busy with their own things, so I just keep it to myself.
What have you dropped or avoided lately that you wish you still did?
I used to go to yoga, but I haven't been in a while. It’s nice to have the time, but I’m just not really missing it.
What do you think changed about how you feel toward yoga?
I don’t know. I think I just got a bit tired of the same routine. It was fun, but it’s not a priority right now.
Is it lack of interest or lack of energy — or both?
Maybe a bit of both? I don't have the same energy for it, and I don't really feel the urge to go.
When you say you don't feel the urge, is that something new for you?
Yeah, I guess so. I used to be super motivated to try new things. Now it’s more like, 'I'll get to it eventually.'
When you need to choose, do you get stuck or go back and forth?
A bit, yeah. It takes me a minute to decide. I just take my time and then pick something.
Can you give me an example of a recent time when taking your time to decide felt frustrating?
I was trying to pick a new lipstick. I looked at like 10 options and just couldn’t decide. It was silly, really.
Does even a simple choice feel like too much sometimes?
Yeah, it feels like a mountain sometimes. But I know it’s not that big a deal, so I just... *sigh*... I just get it over with.
When you say you "get it over with," what does that actually look like for you?
I just make the decision and then I'm done. I don't really dwell on it. It’s fine.
